<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title><jats:p>Considering supergravity theory is a natural step in the development of gravity models. This paper follows the “algebraic“ path and constructs possible extensions of the Poincaré and Anti-de-Sitter algebras, which inherit their basic commutation structure. Previously achieved results of this type are fragmentary and show only a limited fraction of possible algebraic realizations. Our paper presents the newly obtained symmetry algebras, evaluated within an efficient pattern-based computational method of generating the so-called ‘resonating’ algebraic structures. These supersymmetric extensions of algebras, going beyond the Poincaré and Anti-de Sitter ones, contain additional bosonic generators <jats:inline-formula><jats:alternatives><jats:tex-math>$$Z_{ab}$$</jats:tex-math><mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                  <mml:msub>
                    <mml:mi>Z</mml:mi>
                    <mml:mrow>
                      <mml:mi>ab</mml:mi>
                    </mml:mrow>
                  </mml:msub>
                </mml:math></jats:alternatives></jats:inline-formula> (Lorentz-like), and <jats:inline-formula><jats:alternatives><jats:tex-math>$$U_a$$</jats:tex-math><mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                  <mml:msub>
                    <mml:mi>U</mml:mi>
                    <mml:mi>a</mml:mi>
                  </mml:msub>
                </mml:math></jats:alternatives></jats:inline-formula> (translational-like) added to the standard Lorentz generator <jats:inline-formula><jats:alternatives><jats:tex-math>$$J_{ab}$$</jats:tex-math><mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                  <mml:msub>
                    <mml:mi>J</mml:mi>
                    <mml:mrow>
                      <mml:mi>ab</mml:mi>
                    </mml:mrow>
                  </mml:msub>
                </mml:math></jats:alternatives></jats:inline-formula> and translation generator <jats:inline-formula><jats:alternatives><jats:tex-math>$$P_{a}$$</jats:tex-math><mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                  <mml:msub>
                    <mml:mi>P</mml:mi>
                    <mml:mi>a</mml:mi>
                  </mml:msub>
                </mml:math></jats:alternatives></jats:inline-formula>. Our analysis includes all cases up to two fermionic supercharges, <jats:inline-formula><jats:alternatives><jats:tex-math>$$Q_{\alpha }$$</jats:tex-math><mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                  <mml:msub>
                    <mml:mi>Q</mml:mi>
                    <mml:mi>α</mml:mi>
                  </mml:msub>
                </mml:math></jats:alternatives></jats:inline-formula> and <jats:inline-formula><jats:alternatives><jats:tex-math>$$Y_{\alpha }$$</jats:tex-math><mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                  <mml:msub>
                    <mml:mi>Y</mml:mi>
                    <mml:mi>α</mml:mi>
                  </mml:msub>
                </mml:math></jats:alternatives></jats:inline-formula>. The delivered plethora of superalgebras includes few past results and offers a vastness of new examples. The list of the cases is complete and contains all superalgebras up to two of Lorentz-like, translation-like, and supercharge-like generators <jats:inline-formula><jats:alternatives><jats:tex-math>$$(JP+Q)+(ZU+Y)=JPZU+QY$$</jats:tex-math><mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                  <mml:mrow>
                    <mml:mo>(</mml:mo>
                    <mml:mi>J</mml:mi>
                    <mml:mi>P</mml:mi>
                    <mml:mo>+</mml:mo>
                    <mml:mi>Q</mml:mi>
                    <mml:mo>)</mml:mo>
                    <mml:mo>+</mml:mo>
                    <mml:mo>(</mml:mo>
                    <mml:mi>Z</mml:mi>
                    <mml:mi>U</mml:mi>
                    <mml:mo>+</mml:mo>
                    <mml:mi>Y</mml:mi>
                    <mml:mo>)</mml:mo>
                    <mml:mo>=</mml:mo>
                    <mml:mi>J</mml:mi>
                    <mml:mi>P</mml:mi>
                    <mml:mi>Z</mml:mi>
                    <mml:mi>U</mml:mi>
                    <mml:mo>+</mml:mo>
                    <mml:mi>Q</mml:mi>
                    <mml:mi>Y</mml:mi>
                  </mml:mrow>
                </mml:math></jats:alternatives></jats:inline-formula>. In the latter class, among 667 founded superalgebras, the 264 are suitable for direct supergravity construction. For each of them, one can construct a unique supergravity model defined by the Lagrangian. As an example, we consider one of the algebra configurations and provide its Lagrangian realization.</jats:p>
title: Resonant superalgebras for supergravity
